items.text: Most law students ask this question backwards.
The legal world is not one job.
The certificate is now the baseline, not the differentiator.

blocks.heading: Private Platform Courses: Lawsikho and the Rest

items.text: Alongside university-run programs, a set of private legal-education platforms now runs shorter, more current courses aimed squarely at students and young lawyers: LawSikho, LawMarg, Fox Mandal & Associates' short IP course, IALA's live sessions on the DPDP Act and AI, and The Legal School's library of recorded contract drafting, M&A, IBC, and cyber law courses.

LawSikho in particular has built a reputation as one of the largest platforms specifically for Indian law students, running courses like its six-month Diploma in Domestic and International Commercial Arbitration alongside shorter certificate tracks, with a built-in freelance and internship board that tries to turn coursework into paid client work while you study.

Live, practitioner-taught sessions on very current topics (AI contract review, DPDP compliance, legal freelancing), assignment-based feedback, and, at LawSikho specifically, an internal freelance and internship board that can turn coursework into real, paid client work while you are still studying.

blocks.heading: AI Actually Changes for a Young Lawyer

items.text: AI is genuinely useful in legal work right now for search, first-pass summarising of long judgments, and drafting a rough first version of a routine document.

A newer, genuinely useful layer here is legal-tech and AI-literacy for law: knowing how to use AI tools to speed up research and first drafts, and, just as important, knowing how to verify their output rather than trust it blindly.

Treat AI fluency as one layer of a wider high-value skill portfolio , domain knowledge plus AI-assisted speed plus your own verification judgment, not as a shortcut that replaces learning the underlying law.

blocks.heading: Global Certificate Courses Worth the Money

items.text: HarvardX: Contract Law, From Trust to Promise to Contract (edX), a genuinely rigorous, free-to-audit look at the doctrinal foundations of contract law, useful if you want a global, common-law lens on top of Indian contract law.
CopyrightX (Harvard Law School, via HarvardX), a well-regarded, structured course on copyright law with a global perspective, useful for anyone seriously pursuing IPR.

Coursera's legal research, contract, and AI-in-law offerings , quality varies by instructor and university; check the specific course's syllabus, instructor credentials, and recent reviews rather than picking by platform name alone.

blocks.heading: Near-Free Ways to Build the Same Proof

items.text: Channels built specifically for Indian law students, Avani Bansal's plain-language explainers, NALSAR University of Law's faculty lecture uploads, and LawSikho's own free interview and doubt-clearing sessions, cover real, current legal topics at no cost.

Bare Acts, Supreme Court and High Court judgments on official portals, and free case summaries build the same research muscle a paid research-method course teaches, just slower and with less structured feedback.

A moot court problem, a research assistantship for a professor, or volunteering to draft one real document for a legal aid clinic often teaches more applied skill than a recorded course, and it is free.
